title: cw/2, one block at a time
summary: The second version of the walkthrough format replaces a step's fixed slots with an ordered list of blocks. This walkthrough is one of each, so a reader can be checked against something that uses all of them.

parts.title: Words
parts.summary: Two blocks that hold sentences, and the small amount of markup they take.

sections.title: Prose and asides
sections.summary: A markdown block is the paragraph a step is built around. A callout is the sentence that would otherwise start with a warning.

steps.title: A markdown block is the prose

blocks.text: In cw/1 a step had one `body` and four optional slots, and the page decided what order they came in. A cw/2 step has **blocks**, in the order they were written, as many as it needs. ## The markdown a reader has to handle - paragraphs, and *emphasis* inside them - lists, this one included, one level of nesting deep: - like this - fenced code, for the times the code is not a snippet of anything: ```json { "type": "markdown", "text": "..." } ``` > And a quote, for when the words are somebody else's. --- That list is the whole of it. Anything past it a reader shows as the characters that are there, which is allowed and is what keeps `` a piece of text.
Two markdown blocks in a row are two paragraphs the author chose to separate. That is the point of the list: it can say things the slots could not.
cw/1 had one callout and no way to say how much it mattered. cw/2 has four levels, and a title when the first line needs to be short.
Info is the default, and the one to reach for when the sentence is context rather than a warning.

blocks.title: Worth knowing
blocks.text: A tip is something that saves the reader time, not something that saves them from a mistake.
A warning is about something that will go wrong later if it is not noticed now.
Danger is for the thing that deletes data or lets somebody in. Use it about twice a year.

parts.title: Code
parts.summary: Snippets with a place in a file, snippets without one, and the difference between them.

sections.title: Snippets
sections.summary: A snippet with a source is a claim about a real file. A snippet without one is an illustration, and cw/2 wants that difference stated rather than guessed.

steps.title: A snippet that came from somewhere

blocks.text: This one names its file and the line it starts on, so a reader holding the repository can check it and say whether it is still true. `endLine` and the hash are left out here and filled in by `cw migrate` or `cw publish`, because nobody should type a sha256 by hand.

snippet.label: The one field every cw/2 document must have

annotations.text: A constant, not a pattern. A document is one version or the other, and a reader that does not know the value refuses the file.

blocks.text: The highlight and the annotation both point at line 2, and line 2 is the second line of the snippet rather than line 15 of the file. That is the change: move the excerpt up a file and one number changes instead of all of them.

steps.title: A snippet that came from nowhere

blocks.text: No source means no claim. Pseudocode, a shape, a config fragment: leave source out and nothing will tell the reader it went stale, because it was never in a file to begin with.

steps.title: A diff has two sides and knows both

blocks.text: cw/1 wrote a diff as a flat list of lines with one starting number for both sides, which is enough to draw and not enough to be right. cw/2 uses the coordinates a unified diff actually has.

blocks.caption: What the step struct lost, and what it gained.

blocks.text: `oldLines` is 6 because the hunk has three context lines and three deleted ones. `newLines` is 4: the same three context lines and one added one. A validator checks that arithmetic, because the counts are the half of a diff nobody ever looks at and therefore the half that rots.

parts.title: Pictures
parts.summary: A diagram that links to code, a timeline of complete frames, and the one door out of the format.

sections.title: Drawn things
sections.summary: Both of these existed in cw/1 and both were tied to the step they sat in. In cw/2 they point at blocks by name.

steps.title: A diagram links to a block

blocks.text:
flowchart LR
  doc[walkthrough.json] --> version{version}
  version -->|cw/1| one[render1]
  version -->|cw/2| two[render2]
blocks.alt: A document flows into a version check, which chooses between the cw/1 reader and the cw/2 reader.
blocks.caption: The version is read before anything else, because everything else depends on it.

blocks.text: Clicking the version shape opens the code block earlier in this walkthrough. In cw/1 a diagram carried its own copy of the code, which meant the same lines were pasted twice and went stale separately.

steps.title: A timeline is a run of complete pictures

frames.label: Read
frames.note: The bytes arrive, and the version is the first thing looked at.

frames.label: Validate
frames.note: The version picked a schema, and the schema decides whether this goes any further.

frames.label: Inspect
frames.note: What a schema cannot say: that the counts add up and the links point at something.

frames.label: Render
frames.note: The same version choice reaches the browser, which loads one renderer and not the other.

blocks.text: Every frame names every node. That is what lets a reader jump to the third frame without having drawn the first two, and it is why a frame that leaves a node out is a broken frame rather than an implied one.

steps.title: An extension carries its own way out

blocks.text: Every other block type is core, and a type this format has never heard of is an invalid document rather than an extension. `extension` is the one place to put something the format has no opinion about.

blocks.name: roesink/queue-simulator
blocks.fallback: Two workers take five tasks off one queue, one task at a time each. The point is that task four starts before task three finishes.

blocks.text: This reader has never heard of `roesink/queue-simulator`, so it shows the fallback. That is the deal: an extension that does not carry a sentence a reader can print is not an extension, it is a hole.
